evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep skips the 10-15 minute time-boxed framing and 'dependable quote' promise entirely; asks 'Do you have about ten minutes to run through that with me?' then immediately pivots to concerns without confirming a yes or establishing what the call will deliver.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Rep asks: 'Before I kinda hop in here, do you have any, just top of mind, questions or concerns that I could address right off the top.' This is before logistics probing and customer responds with their packing/coverage concern.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raises concern about whether TVs and electronics need to be packed. Rep responds: 'So what is standard service for us is we will come in and rack at protect every single piece of furniture that's including TVs devices...' and then explains the packing option vs. standard service. Customer then asks about partial packing: 'Can they still help me with that or is it just like they do all or they do just moving?' Rep goes deeper: 'No, no, no, absolutely. So what I would do in that case is I would recommend putting like a partial pack...' This shows real two-layer follow-up on concerns raised.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: Rep says: 'So, yeah, that's standard' and 'So just, so I'm hearing you clearly, we won't be adding any additional time for packing, like box packing for you but, but as far as the disassembling reassembling. Nope, that's already computed in the time.' Rep does attempt a reflective summary but it is brief and does not fully recap all concerns or confirm completeness.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Rep covers: property type (apartment with elevator), unit number (1377), destination unit (307), bed type and disassembly, TV size (55 inches), TV stand, plants, L-shaped couch, balcony furniture, chairs, bar stools, side tables, mirror, and miscellaneous items. All major logistics items are discussed.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Rep explicitly offers: 'So the packing option is if you wanted us to come in and you didn't want to do anything like we're coming in we're putting things into boxes we are like doing everything and then moving you. So that would be the packing option.'
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Rep never asks about typical box count or overflow (china, book collections, etc.).
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep provides time ranges: '2.5 to 3.5 hours' for no packing, '6 to 7 hours' with full packing, then '3 to 4 hours,' then '3.5 to 4.5 hours' as final. These are range anchors but never a typical box count or anchored to home size. Personalization occurs (disassembly time added, plant consideration, building familiarity noted) but the estimate itself is time-based, not a dollar range.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Rep mentions 'you only pay for the time you use' multiple times and references the hourly model but never discloses trip fee, overnight fee, packing materials cost, or the '2.5-hour minimum / 15-minute increments' commitment framing. Fee transparency is absent.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Rep never asks 'Does that feel fair?' or any version of it. No pause for customer reaction to pricing.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Rep states: 'And then if for whatever reason we don't arrive within that timeslot and money is automatically deducted off your final bill, which is always nice.' This covers the discount terms clearly.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Rep states: 'I do have your items in here. Can you think of anything else that might be important to note? ... what is also included in this is the know, where we damage coverage that's gonna cover-up to $2,000 for any kind of incidentals which is always nice.' The $2,000 coverage is mentioned but the 'no deductible / no fine print' framing is missing, and it is not explicitly stated that this is built into the rate (not an add-on).
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Rep says 'And then that is pretty much it' and 'Well if you think of anything that you need you have a question on...' but does not ask a version of 'Does that put those to rest?' and does repeat/re-explain some already-covered items (damage coverage, arrival window, 'Meet Your Mover' email).
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Rep asks: 'Can you think of anything else that might be important to note?' This is a weak catch-all, not a genuine 'What's still concerning you about this move?' or similar. It reads as a throwaway checklist item.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Rep asks: 'Can you think of anything else that might be important to note?' which is similar to the catch-all intent, though not the exact wording from the script.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep never asks 'Would you like our help with your move?' or any direct booking request. The call ends with 'Well if you think of anything that you need you have a question on or you need help with my name is Shani please don't hesitate to reach out...' and customer says 'Perfect, Harley, thank you so much.' No explicit ask for the business.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Rep never mentions rate-lock or no-deposit terms.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Rep confirms: arrival window ('1:00 and 1:30'), current unit number ('1377'), destination unit number ('307'), and items/notes. Phone number, date (mentioned in opening but not re-confirmed in booking), crew size, and crew notes about customer concerns are not fully confirmed in the booking section.

top_strength: Excellent two-layer discovery on customer concerns: the rep dug into packing options, partial packing scenarios, furniture disassembly, and special items (plants, TV stand) with follow-up questions that uncovered the exact scope needed rather than accepting surface answers.
coaching_note: Never asked 'Would you like our help with your move?' — the call ended without an explicit booking ask, leaving the sale hanging; always close with a plain, direct ask for the business before confirming details.
